unresolved: Disposition aggregate_only: the source is a retrospective single-centre series of 13 patients treated with CytoSorb hemoadsorption, reported only as medians, means, confidence intervals, counts and percentages; no patient has individual identity evidence or an individually described course, so no individual patient records are created and cohort statements are not copied to placeholder patients. Singleton subgroups (the one non-male patient, the one patient transferred from another hospital's ICU, the one patient without bilateral imaging pathology, the one patient with a single and the one with four hemoadsorption sessions) are each described by a single attribute; the source never links them to one another or to any course, so they are not individuated.
reported_individual_count is 13 (literal) and roster_complete is false because none of the 13 stated individuals can be enumerated.
The age is printed two ways: Table 1 gives a median age of 62 [48-67] years while the results text gives a mean age of 57 (±11) years; these are different summary statistics and are not reconciled.

The time from symptom onset to admission is printed as a mean of 5.9 (95% CI: 4.11-7.55) days to admission to the Emergency Department in the text and as 5.8 (3.8-7.8) days for onset of symptoms before admission in Table 1; the confidence intervals also differ, so this is not a simple rounding difference, and the source does not state that the two are the same measurement. Not reconciled; neither value is used as a label.

The abstract gives p = 0.14 for the change in norepinephrine requirement, while Table 3 prints p = 0.48 for norepinephrine; the abstract p = 0.58 for PaO2/FiO2 is not printed in a table. Not reconciled.

The text says all recorded laboratory parameters and the SOFA score except leukocyte count showed non-significant changes, while Table 2 prints p = 0.03 for the SOFA score; Table 2 also prints some p-values as ">0.01". Not reconciled. The ">0.01" values (leukocytes in Table 2, daily fluid balance in Table 3) are printed beside the two changes the text treats as significant, so a one-character print artefact is possible; recorded as printed. The SOFA score row is also printed under the Arterial blood gases subheading of Table 2.
The text states that the only significant change in Table 3 was the negative fluid balance, while Table 3 prints p = 0.03 for dobutamine (n = 4, median 0.0 at both time points). Not reconciled.
Table 2 prints bilirubin in mmol/L (n = 3) with T_B 11.0 [10.0-333.0] and T_A 106.0 [30.0-182.0]; the unit and spread are kept as printed and not corrected.

Survival is described as all patients alive at the end of hemoadsorption and 72 h after initiation, four patients surviving 28 days, 3 patients (23.1%) discharged alive (abstract: only 3 survived hospital stay), 10 non-survivors versus 3 survivors and an observed mortality of 77% in the discussion; these counts are mutually consistent (28-day and discharge are different time points), and which patients they were is not stated.
Figure 1 (A and B) shows group-level box-plots; values printed on its axes are pixel content and are recorded only in visual.json, never read from plot geometry.
No supplements are listed by the source.
